content.rule: Present Perfect Tense with Time Markers
content.explanation: The present perfect tense (have/has + past participle) connects past actions to present results. It is frequently used with markers like since, for, just, already, yet, never, and ever.

content.rule: Fronting for Emphasis in Formal Writing
content.explanation: Fronting involves placing a time phrase, result/cause clause, or contrasting phrase at the beginning of a sentence to add emphasis and variety in formal texts.

content.passage: Every year, millions of people around the world wait for events like Black Friday to go shopping. They feel excited as they plan their purchases in advance and believe they are making smart choices. But are they really saving money, or are they falling for a set of very clever tricks? One of the most common tricks is called loss aversion. Imagine a jacket that costs 400 Egyptian pounds. You do not really need it. Then a sign appears: 'Was 800 LE, Now 400 LE, Save 50%!' Suddenly, the jacket feels much more attractive. Your brain tells you, 'If I don't buy it, I will lose the chance to save 400 pounds.' Of course, you have not lost anything, but that is how our brains work. Not buying something feels like a loss.

content.correctAnswer: Because loss aversion tricks the brain into viewing not buying it as losing 400 LE
